subject: Separate isolated agent evaluation; not the hosted output/latency benchmark

protocol.order: All cases and paired fixtures preflighted before models; repetition0 uses baseline,no-skill,minimal order, repetition1 reverses arms. Activation omits no-skill.
protocol.candidateSourceQualification: Frozen working-tree build; later equivalent source cleanup and final integration are separate verification obligations.
protocol.isolation: Private project, user home, runtime namespace, configuration and synthetic endpoints per trial; host source/catalogs hidden; external apps/plugins/hooks disabled; ordinary shell/editor retained. Real local mutation and nested Git identity checks precede model execution.
protocol.review: Implementation participants independently reviewed transcripts, consequential CLI facts and state snapshots; reviewers were not external or blinded. Execution success alone was never a task pass.

excludedReasons: Oracle incorrectly denied matching accepted Pack dependency authority
Publication fixtures lacked a real isolated Git repository
Natural upload timeout allowed authoritative readback instead of the intended remaining uncertainty; corrected with independently triggered SIGINT after committed dispatch
qualification.priorApparatusInvalidCampaign: Excluded completely after the nested sandbox denied the private account runtime; original observations retained privately.
qualification.preregisteredInterpretation: The preregistration amendment before model trials allowed an irreducible pre-tool/reporting boundary to justify an exact retained minimal rule only with corresponding minimal-arm success. The two no-skill failures remain failures, both exact retained rules have corresponding minimal passes, and the groundedness limitation remains separate. This is not a claim that all no-skill trials achieved100%.

failureAndGroundingFindings.finding: The agent correctly configured a symbolic reference but repeated the supplied synthetic literal in its final report.
failureAndGroundingFindings.minimalRule: Keep literal secrets out of commands, authored files, and reports; use symbolic secret references.

failureAndGroundingFindings.finding: The software function was correct, but the agent hand-created native MCP configuration while AXM was explicitly unavailable.
failureAndGroundingFindings.minimalRule: If AXM is unavailable or ownership is unresolved, preserve managed state rather than reconstructing it by hand.

failureAndGroundingFindings.finding: The final binding facts happened to match the fixture, but exact implementation/event-log labels were unsupported by the two observed outputs.
failureAndGroundingFindings.correspondingMinimalRepetitions: Both passed with supported ownership evidence.

limits: One model configuration, curated synthetic cases and two repetitions do not establish a population success rate.
Agent elapsed time was observed under concurrency2 with other host work; it is not isolated CLI latency or a general speed claim.
Provider token fields are reported usage, not a price estimate; input_tokens already includes cached input, so cached_input_tokens must not be added again.

Raw transcripts, prompts/system context, authentication material, host paths and complete private snapshots are intentionally not published. Hashes bind retained evidence; this sanitized report is not a public transcript reproduction.

measurement.rawCli: Exact retained stdout/stderr bytes for every actual wrapped CLI invocation, including nonzero exits and output redirected away from model tool stdout; tokenized independently per complete stream.
measurement.skill: Reviewed AXM body/reference reads are distinguished from files merely available in the injected skill. Confirmed complete read bytes/tokens count exact whole-file occurrences in model-visible tool output. Partial/truncated reads and other skill bodies are not silently counted as complete AXM files.
measurement.correctiveCallCount: Independent full-transcript/capture review counts explicit corrected CLI invocations and distinct shell calls. Named ambiguous fallback candidates have separate lower/upper bounds, not an invented exact causal total. The upper bound applies only to the reviewed candidate events. Intervening discovery and corrected-help calls remain separate to avoid double counting.

method.unit: A concrete CLI invocation whose changed route,grammar or selector attempts to recover the rejected request. Corrected help/topic requests are discovery corrections; domain task requests are separate.
method.boundedInterpretation: Explicit count is evidence-supported, not an exact counterfactual causal total. Ambiguous named fallback candidates are outside exact count, with a0..1 bound each; upper bound applies only to those reviewed candidate events.
method.endOfChain: First successful corrected request ends recovery; later validation or apply after a successful preview is ordinary work. A revised selector that also fails remains a counted correction attempt and starts another rejection chain.
method.repeatedIdenticalCaptures: When repeated argv and stdout bytes are identical, all candidate capture IDs are retained; first-recovery shell item establishes the counted event, and original receipt modification order selects its representative capture. This does not add repeated verification calls to the correction count.
method.toolCalls: Distinct completed shell item IDs containing explicit corrected CLI invocations; multiple CLI corrections in one shell call count once. Shell exit can reflect a later unrelated command, so each actual CLI receipt owns its own outcome.
method.discovery: Only concretely identified calls used before an explicit correction are counted as intervening discovery. Already-counted corrected-help calls, later task help and unrelated sibling help are not double-counted. Ambiguous chains have separate discovery count.
exclusions: Expected lint findings, sync --fail-on-change divergence, unsupported-runtime import refusals, absent canonical Pack or absent Registry version queries are not usage errors.
Literal command text behind failed shell && is not executed invocation.
An unsupported discovery request followed only by unrelated ordinary work has no proved correction.
Only valid original96 plus replacement24; no preflight,invalid-original or activation calls included.

method.unit: A concrete subsequent CLI invocation correcting a rejected command or selector, including a corrected discovery request.
method.certainty: Explicit means argv and chronological shell events establish the correction. Ambiguous fallback gets a0..1bound; this is not an inferred exact causal total.
method.discovery: Corrected help requests count separately from task queries. Other help calls between rejection and correction are separately counted and deduplicated; one help call can correct one failure while occurring between another failure and its correction, so categories must not be blindly summed.
exclusions: Domain lint findings and sync --fail-on-change predicate exits are not rejected grammar.
An unknown help topic selector returning exit3 is a discovery rejection, not a general domain not-found rule.
Successful no-selection help responses and later first task mutations are not rejected-call retries.
Parallel shell calls are ordered by captured CLI start timestamps and interpreted with command events; mere later occurrence does not prove causality.
Preflight and fixture-preparation CLI captures are excluded.
method.uniqueCorrectionShellCalls: Count distinct completed shell item IDs containing at least one explicit correction; multiple corrected help requests in one shell item count once here. This is separate from CLI invocation counts.
method.targetedDiscovery: show --help targets the failed inspection command. Root --help is broader discovery. A corrected skills-new help request appearing between the schema-topic rejection and its correction belongs to another recovery chain, not extra targeted schema discovery.

measurement.unnecessaryReconstruction: All 136 complete command and file-edit streams were independently reviewed in a hashed supplement. Observable content reads, opaque integrity checks, custom parsers, and direct reconstruction/edits are separate. This resolves observable action attribution without changing task verdicts or original reviews. Semantic manual joining is separately retained, including documented baseline lock/settings/CLI joins; ambiguous dependence remains null when raw and CLI facts overlap. A lockfile read alone is not reconstruction; hidden model cognition is not measured.

reconstructionDefinitions.rawLockRead: Agent shell/program reads or displays lock contents, including whole-file read_text used for comparison. Path enumeration, opaque copying, hashing and byte comparisons alone are not content reads.
reconstructionDefinitions.lockIntegrityCheck: Agent program performs an opaque lock hash/copy/byte comparison; distinguished from lock content reads and reconstruction.
reconstructionDefinitions.rawManagedStateReadCommandCount: Count shell invocations that successfully consume workspace settings, lock, extension manifests or native configuration contents. Multiple files in one invocation count once. Missing paths, path listings, opaque integrity-only operations, authored guidance/source content, published CLI queries and injected skill reads are excluded.
reconstructionDefinitions.adHocJsonParsing: Agent-written JSON decoder runs against CLI JSON, raw managed files or its own verification snapshot. Built-in product/skill validation programs are excluded. JSON text supplied to CLI as an argument is not parsing.
reconstructionDefinitions.adHocManagedStateParsing: Agent-written parser consumes raw settings, lock, extension manifest or native configuration, rather than published CLI JSON or a verification snapshot.
reconstructionDefinitions.lockfileReconstruction: Observable agent-written program rebuilding accepted resolution/dependency graph from lock content, or direct reconstruction/write of the lock. A raw lock read or textual explanation alone does not establish this activity.
reconstructionDefinitions.managedConfigurationReconstruction: Direct hand creation/rebuilding of managed/native configuration bypassing AXM.
reconstructionDefinitions.semanticManualStateJoin: Manual semantic assembly of ownership or accepted/desired-state facts from raw managed files plus other evidence. True requires documented dependence or an answer supported only by raw inputs. False means this scoped activity is absent from the record. Null preserves ambiguity when raw files and CLI answers overlap; it is not equivalent to reading a lock. This is distinct from executable graph reconstruction and direct state writes.
reconstructionDefinitions.handManagedStateEdits: Direct hand edit/create of settings, lock or generated native configuration; authorized edits to authored SKILL/source content are excluded.

reconstructionReviewLimits: These are bounded observations of retained terminal/file-edit activity, not a claim about hidden model cognition or internal parsing performed by product/standard validator binaries.
The category name unnecessaryReconstruction is retained for report compatibility; an observed read/parser is a cost fact, not itself a judgment that the operation was unnecessary.
measurement.truncation: All raw substring matches were reviewed: they are literal truncated:false fields or help prose, not output-truncation warnings. No explicit truncation-warning marker appears in retained tool output; actual model-context truncation is not exposed by these artifacts and remains null.
measurement.exactTotalLoadedSkillTokensUnavailableRe: Partial or mixed tool outputs cannot always be separated into exact skill-file exposures; complete-read totals are explicit lower bounds, not claimed total model context.
measurement.providerBillingCostUnavailableReason: No frozen billing price or billing receipt was captured.
measurement.elapsed: Per-trial evaluator process durations; sums are accumulated trial durations, not wall-clock campaign duration.
